When I told her that the world doesn't revolve around her, I was probably trying to assert some boundaries and make her understand that her actions and feelings aren't the only important ones. But is that the right approach? Did I handle the situation well? I should think about the possible consequences of my actions. On one hand, telling her that the world doesn't revolve around her could be seen as a way to encourage her to be more considerate of others' feelings and needs. It might help her develop a more balanced perspective. On the other hand, it could come across as dismissive or hurtful, especially if she's already feeling insecure or misunderstood. This suggests that she might not have taken my words constructively. Instead, she might have felt attacked or disrespected, which could escalate the conflict rather than resolve it.
